title: Records with Garner, Al Hibbler, Parker and JATP that he had forgotten
summary: He recites sessions including Paul Leslie on "How High the Moon" and Parker's 1947 Dial sides.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I had forgotten another Erroll Garner record when he was recording for Mercury. "Blue Skies," "Don't Blame Me," "Full Moon and Empty Arms" and "Memories Of You". What brings that to mind is Milt Holland played drums on that. That was the first time I had ever worked with Milt Holland.
And I see Al Hibbler. I had forgotten I had recorded with him. That was on Aladdin. "I Got It Bad and That Ain't Good," "How Long Blues" and "S'posin."
I've got an old, scratchy copy of that.
And Jazz at the Philharmonic. 'How High The Moon.' That was Paul Leslie, whose real name was Les Paul. He turned it around because of contractual agreements with some other company.
Then later, in '47, this was Charlie Parker, 'Dark Shadows,' 'Bird's Nest,' 'This is Always,' 'Cool Blues'. Earl Coleman sang on 'Dark Shadows' and 'This is Always.'
